proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(N_m\), \(m\in\{0,1\}\), for the two finite role SCMs and \(Q\) for their common observational law on \(\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal A_i\).  For every \(k\in\mathbb Z\), take an independent copy \(N_m^k\), including an independent copy of every private or pairwise-shared exogenous root of \(N_m\).  If \(W_{m,s_i}^k\) denotes role \(s_i\) in copy \(k\), define
\[
 O_{m,i,t}:=W_{m,s_i}^{t-\tau_i},\qquad i\in V,\quad t\in\mathbb Z.
\]
This is well typed because there is exactly one role for coordinate \(i\), so \(O_{m,i,t}\in\mathcal A_i\), rather than in a product enlargement of \(\mathcal A_i\).

Consider a finite-role directed edge \(s_j\to s_i\).  Its lag is \(\ell=\tau_i-\tau_j\in\{0,\ldots,L\}\) by hypothesis.  At process time \(t\), the structural equation for \(O_{m,i,t}\) uses \(O_{m,j,t-\ell}\), and the copy indices agree because
\[
 (t-\ell)-\tau_j=t-(\tau_i-\tau_j)-\tau_j=t-\tau_i.
\]
The identical calculation realizes a shared root between two roles at the stipulated offset.  Thus all directed and shared-root spans are at most \(L\), establishing the refinement-span condition.  Positive-lag arrows strictly increase time, while the lag-zero coordinate union is acyclic by premise; hence every instantaneous slice is acyclic.  The structural tables are independent of \(t\), so the equations are time homogeneous.  Every exogenous root belongs to one copy, roots from distinct copies are independent, and every root still has at most two observed children.  Thus the semi-Markovian condition is preserved.  Finally, translating every finite-role edge through all \(t\) gives, by premise, exact summary \(H\).  These observations establish all graphical and structural parts of membership in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).

For strict stationarity, shifting every process time by \(h\) replaces every copy index \(t-\tau_i\) by \(t-\tau_i+h\).  The copies are identically distributed and independent over \(\mathbb Z\), so this relabeling leaves every finite-dimensional distribution unchanged.

It remains to prove equality and positivity of the entire process laws, rather than of a selected window.  Let \(D\subseteq V\times\mathbb Z\) be finite and let \(a_D\) be an assignment.  For every copy index \(k\), put
\[
 D_k:=\{s_i:(i,t)\in D,\ t-\tau_i=k\}.
\]
Only finitely many \(D_k\) are nonempty.  Independence across copies gives, for \(m=0,1\),
\[
 P_{M_m}\{O_{m,D}=a_D\}
 =\prod_{k:D_k\ne\varnothing}Q\{W_{D_k}=a_{D_k}\}.
\]
The right-hand side is independent of \(m\), proving equality on all finite cylinders.  Cylinder sets form the defining coordinate events of the common product space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), so the two process measures are equal.  Each factor is a marginal cell of the strictly positive joint law \(Q\), hence is positive; consequently every finite cylinder has positive probability.

Because \(\tau_X=-\gamma\), the intervened process variable \(O_{m,X,-\gamma}\) is precisely role \(s_X\) in copy \(0\).  Because \(\tau_Y=0\), \(O_{m,Y,0}\) is role \(s_Y\) in that same copy.  The intervention changes no equation in another copy.  Therefore
\[
 P_{M_m}(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =P_{N_m}(s_Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(s_X=x)).
\]
The two quantities on the right differ by premise.  This proves the claimed separation and completes membership in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).

Put \(A_t=O_{1,t}\), \(B_t=O_{2,t}\), and \(C_t=O_{3,t}\), and for \(s\in(0,1)\) define \(b_s(d)=s^d(1-s)^{1-d}\), \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  All variables are binary by \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\).  The two-sided structural solutions exist and are unique causal functions of the noise histories.  Indeed, model zero obeys
\[
 B_t=(R_t\wedge B_{t-1})\oplus U_t\oplus N_t,
\]
and model one obeys
\[
 A_t=(R'_t\wedge A_{t-1})\oplus U'_t\oplus N'_t.
\]
At every time with \(R_t=0\), respectively \(R'_t=0\), the right side forgets the preceding state.  Such reset times occur infinitely often backward almost surely because the reset indicators are independent with probability \(1/2\).  Starting at the most recent reset before \(t\) therefore defines the state at \(t\), and two candidate causal solutions agree after that reset.  The construction commutes with time shifts.

In model zero, conditional on the complete observed past, \(U_t\) is an independent fair bit.  Hence, for every \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})
 &=P_{M_0}(A_t=a\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})
   P_{M_0}(N_t=a\oplus b)\\
 &=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first factor is \(1/2\) even after conditioning on \(R_t\) and \(B_{t-1}\), because XOR with the independent fair bit \(U_t\) is fair.  In model one the same argument makes \(B_t\) fair conditional on the past, and \(A_t=B_t\oplus N'_t\); therefore
\[
 P_{M_1}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
It follows in either model that \((A_t,B_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) is an independent sequence with common mass
\[
 \pi(a,b)=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
Moreover, in both models,
\[
 P(C_t=c\mid (A_s,B_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z},(C_s)_{s<t})=b_r(c\oplus B_{t-1}).
\]
Thus both models have the same complete stationary representation: draw the pairs \((A_t,B_t)\) independently with mass \(\pi\), draw \(E_t\) independently with success probability \(r\), and set \(C_t=B_{t-1}\oplus E_t\).  For example, the probability of a full cylinder on an interval \([u,v]\) is
\[
 \sum_{b_{u-1}\in\{0,1\}}\frac12
 \prod_{t=u}^{v}\pi(a_t,b_t)b_r(c_t\oplus b_{t-1}),
\]
with summation over any unspecified coordinates.  This formula is identical for the two models and is invariant under translating \([u,v]\).  Hence their laws agree on every cylinder and therefore as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and both are strictly stationary.  Since \(q=1/5\) and \(r=1/10\), every displayed factor is positive; in fact every complete one-step cell is at least \((1/2)\min(q,1-q)\min(r,1-r)=1/100\).  Marginalizing shows full finite-cylinder positivity.

The functions also verify exact graph membership.  In model zero, the argument \(B_{t-1}\) changes \(A_t\) whenever \(R_t=1\), \(A_t\) changes \(B_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\) changes \(C_t\).  Its directed edges are therefore \(B_{t-1}\to A_t\), \(A_t\to B_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\to C_t\).  In model one they are \(A_{t-1}\to B_t\), \(B_t\to A_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\to C_t\).  Each instantaneous slice has only one of \(A_t\to B_t\) and \(B_t\to A_t\), so it is acyclic.  All primitive noises are mutually independent, so there are no bidirected edges.  The equations are translation invariant and all lags are at most one.  Both summaries are consequently exactly \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), \(2\to3\), with no bidirected edge.  Together with binary support and the positivity just proved, this establishes \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A)\).

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0)\) in model zero,
\[
 B_{-1}=N_{-1},\qquad C_0=N_{-1}\oplus E_0.
\]
Independence gives
\[
 P_{M_0}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 =q(1-r)+(1-q)r=q+r-2qr
 =\frac15+\frac1{10}-\frac2{50}=\frac{13}{50}.
\]
In model one, \(A_{-1}\) is a child of \(B_{-1}\), while \(B_{-1}\) is fair and is the only observed parent of \(C_0\).  Intervention on \(A_{-1}\) therefore leaves \(B_{-1}\) fair, and
\[
 P_{M_1}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 =\frac12(1-r)+\frac12r=\frac12.
\]
Finally, each effect is separately do-free in its known refinement.  In model zero it is
\[
 \sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}P(C_0=1\mid B_{-1}=b)
 P(B_{-1}=b\mid A_{-1}=0),
\]
because the graph has no hidden common cause and the directed path is \(A_{-1}\to B_{-1}\to C_0\).  In model one there is no directed path from \(A_{-1}\) to \(C_0\), so the effect is \(P(C_0=1)\).  Positivity makes both observational functionals well defined.  This proves refinement-specific identification as well as the claimed common-law collision.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite acyclic directed mixed graph \(\mathcal G\), whenever the recursive ID algorithm returns an expression for \(P_{\mathbf x}(\mathbf y)\), that expression equals the interventional distribution in every semi-Markovian SCM compatible with \(\mathcal G\).

source.verbatim_statement: Whenever ID returns an expression for \(P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})\), it is correct.

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 38 in the JMLR publisher PDF.

added_lemmas.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\).  If the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, let \(G^\star\) contain every directed lag and bidirected offset permitted by \(H\) and \(L\), and let \(A^\star=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})\).  Then \(A^\star\subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]\) and \(|A^\star|\le n(nL+1)\).  If ordinary ID on the finite ADMG \(G^\star[A^\star]\) returns \(F\), then \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) and \(F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Every directed edge of \(G^\star\) goes from time \(t-\ell\) to time \(t\) with \(0\le\ell\le L\).  Projecting a directed path in \(G^\star\) to coordinate labels gives a directed walk in the directed part of \(H\).  Because that graph is acyclic and has no self-loop, a coordinate cannot repeat on this walk.  A directed path into either query vertex therefore contains at most \(n-1\) edges.  Its total backward displacement is at most \((n-1)L\).  Since the query times are \(-\gamma\) and \(0\),
\[
 A^\star\subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0].
\]
There are \(\gamma+(n-1)L+1\le nL+1\) integer times in this interval, where \(0\le\gamma\le L\); hence \(|A^\star|\le n(nL+1)\).

Now fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with refinement \(R\).  Exact-summary compatibility and the refinement-span condition imply \(R\subseteq G^\star\).  The set \(A^\star\) is ancestral in \(G^\star\), so no directed arrow from a vertex outside \(A^\star\) enters it.  Removing the outside observed vertices therefore leaves the structural equations on \(A^\star\) unchanged.  A pairwise exogenous root with only one endpoint remaining becomes a private root; thus the marginal law \(P_M(A^\star)\) is generated by a semi-Markovian SCM whose ADMG is a subgraph of \(G^\star[A^\star]\).  It is consequently compatible with that supergraph.

By \(\mathrm{lem:ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}soundness}\), the expression returned by ordinary ID on \(G^\star[A^\star]\) equals the queried intervention distribution in every such compatible SCM.  Therefore
\[
 F(P_M(A^\star))
 =P_M(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =\theta_M(y;x).
\]
The set \(A^\star\) is finite, so every joint or marginal cell used by ID is a finite cylinder probability on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Finite-alphabet marginalization gives finite sums and products, and any conditional-kernel division has a positive denominator by cylinder positivity.  Hence \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\).  Since \(M\) was arbitrary, the formula is uniform over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For the input \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the family \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)\) is empty, while for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\),
\[
 P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))
 =F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)
 =\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}P_M(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=0,X_0=a)P_M(X_0=a).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Here \(V=\{X,Y\}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\), a certificate must contain a nonempty mediator-role set
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal D\subseteq(V\setminus\{X,Y\})\times[-b,0].
\]
The set on the right is empty, so the certificate family is empty.

Fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\).  Exact summary says that the only possible observed parents of \(Y_0\) are \(X_{-1}\) and \(X_0\), with at least one of those arguments active, and that \(X_t\) has no observed parent.  There is no bidirected summary edge, so semi-Markovianity makes the exogenous root of \(Y_0\) independent of every root generating \(X_{-1}\) and \(X_0\).  It also makes \(X_{-1}\) and \(X_0\) independent; strict stationarity gives them the same marginal law.  Let
\[
 g(u,v):=P_M\{f_Y(u,v,U_{Y,0})=1\},
\]
where an argument is simply omitted if its corresponding lag is absent.  Exogenous independence and cylinder positivity give
\[
 P_M(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=u,X_0=v)=g(u,v).
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0)\), the variable \(X_0\) and the root \(U_{Y,0}\) retain their observational laws.  The truncated structural equations therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))
 &=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}g(0,a)P_M(X_0=a)\\
 &=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}P_M(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=0,X_0=a)P_M(X_0=a)\\
 &=F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M).
 \end{aligned}
\]
All denominators in the displayed conditionals are positive by cylinder positivity.  This proves the claimed identifying map independently of any unconstructed transducer trace.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\mathcal A\) and \(M\), and let \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) use finitely many cylinders.  Assume \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\), strict stationarity, cylinder positivity, \(\beta_M(k)\le C_\beta\rho^k\), the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).  Define \(\widehat\theta_F\) and \(\widehat v_F\) on the event that their empirical denominators are positive, and arbitrarily off that event.  Then that event has probability tending to one,
\[
 \widehat\Omega_F\overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F,\qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_F-\theta_M(y;x))\Rightarrow N(0,v_F),\qquad
 \widehat v_F\overset p\longrightarrow v_F,
\]
and
\[
 P_M\!\left\{\theta_M(y;x)\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}\right]\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Algebraically equivalent cylinder expressions have the same limit after redundant simplex coordinates are removed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \([a_j,b_j]\) be the smallest integer interval containing all time indices in the \(j\)-th cylinder, after placing that cylinder at shift zero, and put \(w=\max_j(b_j-a_j)<\infty\).  Then \(Z_t\) is measurable with respect to the observed variables from time \(t+\min_j a_j\) through time \(t+\max_j b_j\).  Consequently the absolute-regularity coefficients of \((Z_t)\) satisfy
\[
 \beta_Z(k)\le \beta_M((k-w)_+)\le C_\beta\rho^{(k-w)_+}.
\]
Indeed, the past and future sigma fields generated by the two \(Z\)-blocks are subfields of observed-process sigma fields separated by at least \(k-w\), and absolute regularity decreases when sigma fields are restricted.  Since every coordinate of \(Z_t\) lies in \([0,1]\), the total-variation definition of \(\beta\) gives, for bounded scalar functions \(G,H\) of blocks separated by \(k\),
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(G,H)|
 \le4\lVert G\rVert_\infty\lVert H\rVert_\infty\beta_Z(k).
\]
Thus every entry of \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Cov}(Z_0,Z_k)\) is absolutely summable, so \(\Omega_F\) is finite.  The same covariance bound yields
\[
 E\lVert\widehat p_F-p_F\rVert^2=O(T^{-1}),
\]
where omitting the fixed cylinder boundary changes the mean by only \(O(T^{-1})\).  Hence \(\widehat p_F-p_F=O_p(T^{-1/2})\).

For completeness, a blocking argument gives the required multivariate central limit theorem from these stated assumptions.  Fix a vector \(c\) and put \(W_t=c^{\mathsf T}(Z_t-p_F)\).  Let the big-block length be \(b_T=\lfloor T^{1/5}\rfloor\), let the separating gap be \(s_T=\lceil d\log T\rceil\), where \(d>2/|\log\rho|\), and partition \(1,\ldots,T\) into big blocks separated by such gaps.  Absolute covariance summability shows that the variance of the sum over all gaps, divided by \(T\), is \(O(s_T/b_T)=o(1)\).  If \(m_T\) is the number of big blocks, iterative use of the total-variation definition gives, for the joint characteristic function of their sums and the product of their marginal characteristic functions, the bound
\[
 2(m_T-1)\beta_Z(s_T)
 \le C\frac{T}{b_T}\rho^{s_T-w}=o(1).
\]
It therefore suffices to analyze independent random variables having the big-block-sum marginals.  Absolute covariance summability also gives
\[
 \frac1T\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{t=1}^T W_t\right)
 \longrightarrow
 \sigma_c^2:=c^{\mathsf T}\Omega_Fc,
\]
and removing the gaps does not change this limit.  Each centered big-block sum is bounded by \(C b_T\).  Taylor's formula for its characteristic function has total third-order remainder bounded by
\[
 \frac{C b_T}{T^{3/2}}\sum_{j=1}^{m_T}\operatorname{Var}(B_{T,j})
 =O(b_TT^{-1/2})=o(1).
\]
The quadratic terms converge to \(-u^2\sigma_c^2/2\), and their maximal magnitude is \(O(b_T/T)=o(1)\); taking the product therefore yields \(\exp(-u^2\sigma_c^2/2)\).  Restoring the negligible gaps proves
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt T}\sum_{t=1}^T W_t\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma_c^2).
\]
Since \(c\) was arbitrary, the corresponding characteristic-function identity proves
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat p_F-p_F)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_F).
\]

We next prove HAC consistency.  Write \(U_t=Z_t-p_F\), \(\Gamma_k=E(U_tU_{t-k}^{\mathsf T})\), and
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_k=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^TU_tU_{t-k}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For any matrix entry, the product at time \(t\) and the product at time \(t+r\) are bounded.  When \(r>k+w\), their underlying observed blocks are separated by at least \(r-k-w\); the covariance inequality above applies.  For the remaining \(k+w+1\) separations use the bound by one.  Uniformly for \(0\le k<T\),
\[
 E\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_k-E\widetilde\Gamma_k\rVert
 \le C\sqrt{\frac{k+w+1}{T}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 E\sum_{k=0}^{h_T}\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_k-E\widetilde\Gamma_k\rVert
 \le C\frac{h_T^{3/2}}{\sqrt T}=o(1),
\]
because \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).  Also \(E\widetilde\Gamma_k=(1-k/T)\Gamma_k\).  Since \(h_T\to\infty\), the Bartlett weights converge to one at each fixed lag, are bounded by one, and \(\sum_k\lVert\Gamma_k\rVert<\infty\).  Splitting the sum at a fixed lag and then sending that lag to infinity gives
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_0+
 \sum_{k=1}^{h_T}K(k/(h_T+1))
 (\widetilde\Gamma_k+\widetilde\Gamma_k^{\mathsf T})
 \overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F.
\]
Finally, with \(d_T=\widehat p_F-p_F\), replacing \(U_t\) by \(U_t-d_T\) changes each empirical lag covariance by at most \(C(\lVert d_T\rVert+\lVert d_T\rVert^2)\).  Summed over \(h_T\) lags this is \(O_p(h_TT^{-1/2})=o_p(1)\).  Hence \(\widehat\Omega_F\overset p\to\Omega_F\).

Every denominator of \(F\) is positive at \(p_F\).  There are finitely many denominators, so all remain positive on some neighborhood of \(p_F\).  Since \(\widehat p_F\to_p p_F\), the empirical-domain event has probability tending to one.  On this neighborhood the rational map \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable, and Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt T\{F(\widehat p_F)-F(p_F)\}
 =\nabla F(p_F)^{\mathsf T}\sqrt T(\widehat p_F-p_F)+o_p(1).
\]
Using the assumed identifying equality \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\) and the vector central limit theorem yields the stated normal limit with variance
\[
 v_F=\nabla F(p_F)^{\mathsf T}\Omega_F\nabla F(p_F).
\]
Continuity of \(\nabla F\), consistency of \(\widehat p_F\), and HAC consistency imply \(\widehat v_F\to_p v_F\).  Since \(v_F>0\), studentization and continuity of the standard normal distribution give
\[
 P_M\!\left\{\theta_M(y;x)\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}\right]\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]

For the final invariance assertion, remove linearly redundant cylinder cells and use coordinates on the relative interior of the resulting probability simplex.  Algebraically equivalent rational expressions agree on an open subset of those coordinates, so their gradients there agree.  Equivalently, before reduction their gradient difference is normal to the affine support of \(Z_t-p_F\), and hence is annihilated by \(\Omega_F\).  Their linear delta-method terms and quadratic variance forms are therefore identical.

added_lemmas.statement: For a fixed finite family of valid cylinder identifying functionals \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\), suppose each trajectory obeys the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\), and let \(\theta_j=F_j(p_{F_j})\).  If \(\Delta=\min_{j\ne k}|\theta_j-\theta_k|>0\), then the ordering induced by \(\widehat\theta_{F_1},\ldots,\widehat\theta_{F_m}\) equals the population ordering with probability tending to one.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\) implies \(\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j=O_p(T^{-1/2})\), and hence \(\widehat\theta_{F_j}\to_p\theta_j\), for every fixed \(j\).  Since \(m<\infty\), the union bound gives
\[
 P\!\left(\max_{1\le j\le m}|\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j|\ge\Delta/3\right)
 \le\sum_{j=1}^mP\!\left(|\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j|\ge\Delta/3\right)
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
On the complementary event, if \(\theta_j<\theta_k\), then
\[
 \widehat\theta_{F_j}<\theta_j+\Delta/3
 \le\theta_k-2\Delta/3
 <\widehat\theta_{F_k}.
\]
Thus every pairwise comparison, and therefore the full ranking, is correct on an event whose probability tends to one.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Fix \(\mathcal A\).  Let \(S=\{s_i=(i,\tau_i):i\in V\}\) contain exactly one temporal role for each coordinate, with \(s_X=(X,-\gamma)\) and \(s_Y=(Y,0)\).  Suppose two finite temporal-role semi-Markovian SCMs on \(S\) use the alphabets \(\mathcal A_i\), have legal lags bounded by \(L\), have a common strictly positive rational joint role law, have different probabilities of \(s_Y=y\) under \(\operatorname{do}(s_X=x)\), have acyclic unions of lag-zero coordinate relations, and have translation closures with exact common summary \(H\).  Then the independent-shift construction yields \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) such that \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current independent-shift formula places one slot for every temporal role inside a coordinate, so with two roles of a binary coordinate its output alphabet has at least four elements and is not the fixed \(\mathcal A_i\). Auxiliary edge channels enlarge it again. The proposed claim restricts the seed to exactly one role per coordinate and requires exact summary before lifting; on this genuine subclass the construction is well typed and the fixed-alphabet conclusion is proved.

proposed.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\).  Let \(S=\{s_i=(i,\tau_i):i\in V\}\) contain exactly one temporal role for each coordinate, with \(s_X=(X,-\gamma)\) and \(s_Y=(Y,0)\).  Suppose two finite temporal-role semi-Markovian SCMs on \(S\) use the alphabets \(\mathcal A_i\), have legal lags bounded by \(L\), have a common strictly positive rational joint role law, have different probabilities of \(s_Y=y\) under \(\operatorname{do}(s_X=x)\), have acyclic unions of lag-zero coordinate relations, and have translation closures with exact common summary \(H\).  Then the independent-shift construction yields \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) such that \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\).
proposed.justification: This lemma turns a bounded graphical collision into the whole-process stationary countermodels required for semantic nonidentification.
proposed.gap: Shpitser--Pearl construct finite fixed-ADMG hedge models, while Jahn--Karnik--Schulman localize fixed-graph hedges; neither result preserves strict stationarity, time homogeneity, exact summaries, and equality of the entire process law under a refinement switch.
proposed.consumer: Every rejecting state of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\) obtains an auditable finite countermodel on the fixed product alphabet rather than an inconclusive failure code.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This replacement synchronizes the narrowed claim with its exact free symbols and adds the cylinder-positivity premise used in the proof.

proposed.statement: For the fixed binary family in \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\), the two models belong to the same \(\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A)\), have exact common summary \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), \(2\to3\), no bidirected edges, the same strictly positive entire stationary observed law as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and separately identifiable refinement-specific effects, but \(P_{M_0}(O_{3,0}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(O_{1,-1}=0))=13/50\) and \(P_{M_1}(O_{3,0}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(O_{1,-1}=0))=1/2\).
proposed.justification: This positive collision proves that per-refinement ID and formula enumeration are not complete for the uniform query.
proposed.gap: The abstraction hierarchy separates graphwise identification from common identification abstractly; this proposition gives a strictly stationary finite-alphabet micro-effect collision with exact arithmetic and whole-law equality.
proposed.consumer: The example is a mandatory rejection regression test for any implementation and prevents false causal rankings in EasyRCA.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof of class membership uses every defining support, graphical, structural, homogeneity, stationarity, and positivity condition, so those dependencies must be explicit.

proposed.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\). If the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, let \(G^\star\) contain every permitted directed lag and bidirected offset. The ancestors of \(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\}\) in \(G^\star\) lie in \(V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]\), contain at most \(n(nL+1)\) vertices, and one ordinary ID call on this ancestral ADMG is sound and complete for uniform identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with every returned probability evaluated on the common product alphabet.
proposed.justification: The proposition supplies a nontrivial solved subclass and a required reduction test for the general transducer.
proposed.gap: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui use a densest candidate full-time graph to validate adjustment under causal sufficiency, and Jahn--Karnik--Schulman analyze one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph. This reduction instead uses one saturated ancestral ADMG to decide general fixing-based identification uniformly over unknown lag refinements and supplies exact-summary stationary negative witnesses.
proposed.consumer: Acyclic EasyRCA summaries can be screened immediately with an ordinary finite ID implementation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The new helper records the proved ancestor bound and ordinary-ID soundness half and is a direct dependency of the still-open completeness claim.

proposed.statement: For every fixed finite alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), the graphical criterion in Theorem 1 of Assaad (2025) induces an explicit certificate \(c_{\mathrm A}\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma)\). For every \(c\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma)\), \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\) follows the corresponding fixing sequence, returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_c)\), and \(F_c\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) is the generalized front-door functional certified by \(c\); for \(c=c_{\mathrm A}\), this is algebraically Assaad's published functional. For the concrete input \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)=\varnothing\) because there is no non-treatment, non-outcome mediator coordinate, while the complete trace \(\mathfrak t_{\mathrm{out}}\) returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\) and \(F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)=P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\). Hence the successful TID-SCG region strictly contains this generic front-door family, with Assaad's criterion as a proved member.
proposed.justification: The frontier theorem proves universal inclusion for an explicit family of front-door criteria, embeds the published criterion, and supplies a fully traced identified input outside the family.
proposed.gap: Assaad's theorem is one sufficient front-door criterion. The present result proves it is an instance of a larger explicit uniform front-door family, maps every member of that family to a successful transducer certificate, and then verifies strict containment using a lag-one back-door-identified query with no eligible mediator coordinate.
proposed.consumer: EasyRCA can retain every published or generalized SCG front-door identification while certifying additional lag effects, and the five-state trace supplies an executable regression test for that strict gain.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The outside-family emptiness and identifying equality are now a separate proved load-bearing proposition and must be wired into the theorem.

proposed.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\) and condition on \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\). For one stationary trajectory in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), geometric beta mixing and boundedness of the indicators of the finitely many returned cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A,j}\) imply the moment and mixing hypotheses used for Newey--West HAC consistency. With modified Bartlett weights \(1-k/(h_T+1)\), \(h_T\to\infty\), and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), \(\widehat\Omega_F\overset p\to\Omega_F\), \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_F-\theta_M(y;x))\Rightarrow N(0,v_F)\), \(\widehat v_F\overset p\to v_F\), and \(P_M\{\theta_M(y;x)\in[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}]\}\to1-\alpha\). The limit is invariant under algebraically equivalent expressions in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) after redundant simplex coordinates are removed.
proposed.justification: A graphically identified cylinder functional becomes operational only with dependence-aware single-trajectory uncertainty quantification.
proposed.gap: Bhattacharya--Nabi--Shpitser develop hidden-graph influence-function estimators for independent samples, while Viviano--Bradic treat different time-series causal targets; neither gives a generic HAC delta method for overlapping cylinders emitted by a graph algorithm.
proposed.consumer: EasyRCA obtains confidence intervals for identified lag-specific transmission probabilities from one stationary regime.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proved statistical kernel is a direct dependency; the unchanged theorem still also requires the open success-soundness implication.

proposed.statement: For any finite collection of EasyRCA lag-specific transmission queries defined on one fixed coordinate set and alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), rank only pairs for which \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\); if their population scores are separated by a fixed positive margin, the plug-in ranking is consistent, while every failed query is accompanied by its \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A)\) certificate and is excluded rather than assigned a causal score.
proposed.justification: The proposition states the precise consumer contract: identified comparisons are ranked and unresolved comparisons trigger certified abstention.
proposed.gap: EasyRCA assumes jointly independent noises and compares adjustment-based direct effects; it does not propagate latent-confounding identification failures into its ranking.
proposed.consumer: Operators receive a causal ranking only where the summary abstraction supports one, with explicit reasons for missing edges.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The finite-margin ranking argument is now an explicit proved dependency rather than an undeclared consequence.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The completeness direction: turning ordinary-ID failure on the saturated ancestral ADMG into two models in the fixed class \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with the same entire stationary law.
open_obligations.obstruction: An ordinary finite-ADMG hedge can contain several time roles of one coordinate. The advertised independent-shift construction stores those roles as coordinate slots, changing \(\mathcal A_i\) to a product alphabet. Exact-summary padding adds further slots. Therefore the current negative lift does not land in the fixed-alphabet class quantified by this proposition.
open_obligations.attempted: I verified the ancestor bound and supergraph soundness, then audited the negative shift construction at the coordinate, intervention, and outcome-event types. The mismatch occurs before any hedge arithmetic and cannot be repaired by relabeling when, for example, \(|\mathcal A_i|=2\) but two binary slots are required.
open_obligations.partial_result: The ancestor bound and the soundness half are proved in \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}id\text{-}soundness}\): a successful ordinary ID call on at most \(n(nL+1)\) vertices returns one uniform finite-cylinder functional.  What remains unproved is the converse implication from failure of ID on \(G^\star[A^\star]\) to two strictly stationary countermodels on the fixed alphabet family \(\mathcal A\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: A finite offset-sensitive state space, a sound transition relation, a pumping invariant, an explicit bound \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)\), and a rejecting-state construction of a fixed-alphabet positive lag-switch pair.
open_obligations.obstruction: The transducer handle is an instruction to adapt several calculi, not a mathematical construction: it specifies neither states as finite encoded objects nor rewrite rules, invariants, acceptance semantics, or a lag-hedge grammar. No frozen result localizes cross-refinement functional disagreement, and the general stationary lift used by the proposed failure branch is ill typed on fixed alphabets.
open_obligations.attempted: I tested the two obvious reductions. Raw quotient fixing conflates temporal offsets, and per-refinement ordinary ID accepts the proved lag-switch collision. Saturated-graph ID gives a sound acyclic subclass but not a fixed-alphabet negative lift or a cyclic pumping theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result: The finite lag-switch pair in \(\mathrm{prop:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}collision}\) proves that accepting whenever each refinement is individually identifiable is unsound.  The acyclic-summary helper proves a finite radius \(\gamma+(n-1)L\) and uniform soundness in the acyclic directed-summary subclass.  The corrected stationary lift converts only a one-role-per-coordinate finite collision with exact summary into fixed-alphabet stationary countermodels.  No bounded cross-refinement fixing normal form follows from these results.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construction and proof of termination, accepting soundness, rejecting soundness, and completeness of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The procedure and bound are supplied only by the unresolved open-ended normal-form target. Without an accepting invariant a \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}\) token has no proved causal meaning; without a general fixed-alphabet collision lift a \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) token has no certified pair of compatible stationary SCMs.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived the formal consequences that would follow from the two branch invariants and checked the explicit lag-switch rejection witness, but neither step constructs the missing normal form or proves its completeness.
open_obligations.partial_result: Conditional on a normal form having the advertised accepting and rejecting invariants, accepting soundness would follow from its typed cylinder identity and rejecting soundness from a valid fixed-alphabet stationary lift; exclusivity would then follow directly from \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\).  The lag-switch proposition supplies one concrete mandatory rejection.  The missing normal form prevents an unconditional termination bound and completeness implication.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The certificate-indexed generalized front-door functional and fixing proof, the exact mapping of Assaad's Theorem 1 into the stated certificate grammar, and the assertion that the unconstructed transducer follows these sequences and returns them.
open_obligations.obstruction: The definition states graphical clauses but never writes \(F_c\), while the transducer has no transition relation. The outside trace is prose that asserts kernel identities rather than deriving them from defined rules.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved directly that the proposed outside family is empty and that its displayed \(F_{\mathrm{out}}\) identifies the effect uniformly. This does not establish the general front-door clauses or any transducer-return statement.
open_obligations.partial_result: The outside-class part that does not mention the transducer is proved in \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\): the certificate family is empty and \(F_{\mathrm{out}}\) identifies the intervention for every compatible model.  What remains is an explicit general formula \(F_c\), a proof that the stated graphical conditions justify it, a verified embedding of Assaad's theorem, and a constructed transducer whose trace returns it.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Only the implication from a TID-SCG success token to the identifying equality needed to center the limit law at \(\theta_M(y;x)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: That implication is precisely accepting soundness of the unresolved dichotomy. A syntactic \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\) condition alone does not entail \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\) from any established frozen definition or result.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the complete statistical theorem directly from bounded finite-window indicators and geometric absolute regularity, including the mixing CLT, HAC consistency, empirical-denominator event, delta method, Wald coverage, and simplex-coordinate invariance.
open_obligations.partial_result: The entire statistical claim, including the overlapping-window central limit theorem, Bartlett HAC consistency, delta method, studentization, and representation invariance, is proved in \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\) under the explicit identifying equality \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\).  To recover the target exactly, one still needs the unproved implication \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\Rightarrow F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\) from \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The claims about the behavior and failure output of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) when \(L=0\).
open_obligations.obstruction: At \(L=0\) the graph and query reduce to a static slice, but the current core still provides no algorithmic transition rules that can be shown to coincide with ordinary ID. The general stationary-lift lemma used for failure was also false on fixed alphabets and has been narrowed.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced the structural graph and causal query to one static ADMG and checked ordinary-ID soundness. This proves the semantic boundary but not the asserted behavior of an undefined procedure or its certificate encoder.
open_obligations.partial_result: When \(L=0\), every allowed directed or bidirected edge lies within one time slice, and the lag-zero query is therefore the ordinary static query on the slice ADMG \(H\).  Ordinary ID is sound for this query.  The assertion that the presently undefined \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) procedure reduces to ID, and its fixed-alphabet stationary failure-certificate claim, do not follow until the normal form and a suitable negative lift are supplied.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The claims that every success is causally valid and every failure carries the advertised certificate.
open_obligations.obstruction: Both are direct consequences of the unresolved TID-SCG dichotomy. Statistical consistency alone cannot certify the causal interpretation of a returned score or manufacture a rejecting SCM pair.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the finite-margin plug-in ranking argument for any fixed finite family of valid cylinder functionals. The proof isolates precisely the remaining graphical certification step.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any fixed finite collection of valid successful functionals, \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}margin\text{-}plugin\text{-}ranking}\) proves ranking consistency under a positive population margin.  The remaining abstention claim requires the unproved dichotomy to ensure that every \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) token carries a valid lag-switch certificate and that every \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}\) token is identifying.
